newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - LatAm ADRs firm after currency fears.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - LatAm ADRs firm after currency fears.

text.p: Latin American ADRs firmed Wednesday from a sell-off sparked by jitters that Asian currency turmoil could hit Brazil and the rest of the region.

Traders said Latin American ADRs -- American Depositary Receipts -- were being buoyed by the resurgent Brazilian stock exchange. Sao Paulo's high-flying Bovespa index was up 2.8 percent in mid-morning after plunging 8.5 percent Tuesday.
"Things are looking positive," a trader said. "Basically the Latin markets are looking at Brazil, especially the telecommunications stocks, which got hammered yesterday."
He added, "It looks like we found a floor here."
Brazil's bellwether ADR, Telebras SA rose 3-3/8 to 138 and was among the most active issues on the New York Stock Exchange. Telebras fell 11-1/4 Tuesday and is off a high of 169-1/4 Thursday.
Telefonos de Mexico rose 12/16 to 51-9/16 and Venezuela's CANTV telephone company was up 1/4 to 42-1/4.
Among other Latin American ADRs, Argentina's YPF oil company was off 12/16 to 29-11/16 after it sold the 10 percent of its shares held by employees.

Latin American exchanges, among the best-performing markets in the world this year, were hit by a sell-off Tuesday. Stocks slumped amid profit-taking after this year's strong run-up and worries that turmoil that have shaken the Thai, Philippine and Malaysian currencies could jolt Brazil's currency, the real.

The worries were fueled in part by Brazil's longstanding and sizeable current account and trade deficits. Traders said jitters over the current account were eased somewhat by Brazil's decree Wednesday that money from the sale of state companies had to go to debt retirement.
Analysts in New York stressed that Brazil and the rest of Latin America remained fundamentally strong.

"While we believe yesterday's weakness was part of a more general market correction, any weakness specific to Brazil on current account concerns is an opportunity to buy," Lehman Brothers said in an analysis.
Among other ADRs, Nordic telecommunications equipment companies Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson and Nokia Group rose to 12-month highs.
Ericsson rose 1-9/16 to 43-9/16 after Salomon Brothers started coverage of the stock with a buy rating. Nokia was up 3-3/16 to 83-9/16.
